senses.def: heart of palm, palmito: the edible core at the top of a palm stem

examples.text: Palmherzen gibt es meistens im Glas oder in der Dose.
examples.tr: Hearts of palm usually come in a jar or a tin.

examples.text: Das Palmherz schmeckt mild, ein bisschen wie Spargel.
examples.tr: Heart of palm tastes mild, a little like asparagus.

examples.text: In Brasilien isst man Palmherzen im Salat.
examples.tr: In Brazil people eat hearts of palm in salads.

synonyms.nuance: variant with Palmen-
the Spanish/Portuguese name, used in Latin American recipes

etymology.text: Palme (“palm”, from Latin palma) + Herz (“heart”, from Old High German hërza, cognate with English heart).

funFacts: For many wild palms, harvesting the heart kills the tree; today most palm hearts come from farmed multi-stemmed palms such as the peach palm.
pitfalls: Herz is irregular, and so is Palmherz in some forms: genitive des Palmherzes or des Palmherzens, dative dem Palmherz or Palmherzen.
subtleties: Usually used in the plural for the product (Palmherzen); one piece is ein Palmherz or eine Stange Palmherz.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A thin, pale winter root with a mild taste that some find reminiscent of oysters.

senses.def: salsify, oyster plant (Tragopogon porrifolius)

examples.text: Die Haferwurzel ist eine Verwandte der Schwarzwurzel.
examples.tr: Salsify is a relative of black salsify.

examples.text: Haferwurzeln schält man am besten unter Wasser.
examples.tr: It is best to peel salsify roots under water.

examples.text: Heute findet man die Haferwurzel fast nur noch auf dem Wochenmarkt.
examples.tr: Today you find salsify almost only at the farmers’ market.

synonyms.nuance: name from the taste, listed by German Wikipedia
botanical name, after the purple flowers
old regional name

etymology.text: Hafer (“oats”, from Old High German habaro) + Wurzel (“root”, from Old High German wurzala); the leaves look like grass or oat leaves.

funFacts: Haber is the old southern form of Hafer – the folk name Habermark keeps it.
pitfalls: Do not confuse Haferwurzel (white salsify, Tragopogon) and Schwarzwurzel (black salsify, Scorzonera).
subtleties: Like black salsify it exudes a sticky milky sap; gloves or a little vinegar in the water help.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A bundle of sweet white finger-roots from medieval gardens, now a rarity for collectors.

senses.def: skirret (Sium sisarum), a sweet root vegetable of the carrot family

examples.text: Die Zuckerwurzel war im Mittelalter ein beliebtes Gemüse.
examples.tr: Skirret was a popular vegetable in the Middle Ages.

examples.text: Zuckerwurzeln schmecken süßlich und nussig.
examples.tr: Skirret roots taste sweetish and nutty.

examples.text: Die Zuckerwurzel bildet viele dünne Wurzeln.
examples.tr: Skirret forms many thin roots.

synonyms.nuance: short variant
old regional name listed by German Wikipedia

etymology.text: Zucker (“sugar”, from Old High German zuckar, via Italian and Arabic سُكَّر sukkar from Sanskrit śarkarā) + Wurzel (“root”).

funFacts: Pliny wrote that the emperor Tiberius demanded skirret (siser) from Germania every year.
pitfalls: Not the same as Zuckerrübe (sugar beet).
subtleties: The roots grow in a cluster and can have a hard core, which is removed – one reason why the carrot and parsnip replaced it.

plurals.none: a mass noun: used without a plural

profile.feeling: Tiny, pearly, ringed tubers that look like little caterpillars; a delicacy of French cuisine.

senses.def: Chinese artichoke, crosne (Stachys affinis), a mint-family plant with small edible tubers

examples.text: Die Knollen vom Knollenziest sehen aus wie kleine Raupen.
examples.tr: The tubers of the Chinese artichoke look like little caterpillars.

examples.text: Knollenziest muss man nicht schälen.
examples.tr: Chinese artichokes do not need peeling.

examples.text: Auf dem Markt heißt Knollenziest manchmal Crosne.
examples.tr: At the market Chinese artichoke is sometimes called crosne.

synonyms.nuance: folk name listed by German Wikipedia
loan translation, though it is no artichoke
French name used by cooks

etymology.text: Knolle (“tuber”, from Middle High German knolle) + Ziest (“woundwort, Stachys”, 18th century, from Sorbian cysć / čist, from Proto-Slavic *čistъ “pure”).

funFacts: The French name crosne comes from the village of Crosne near Paris, where it was first grown in France in the 1880s.
pitfalls: German Wikipedia writes Knollen-Ziest with a hyphen, the botanical style; cooks write Knollenziest.
subtleties: Used as a mass noun; for single tubers say die Knollen or die Knöllchen.

profile.feeling: Known in Germany mostly as a tiny gluten-free grain; in Greece and Asia the leaves are a summer green.

senses.def: amaranth (Amaranthus), especially its leaves eaten as greens

examples.text: In Griechenland isst man junge Blätter vom Amarant gekocht mit Olivenöl.
examples.tr: In Greece young amaranth leaves are eaten boiled with olive oil.

examples.text: Amarant gibt es im Bioladen meistens als Körner oder gepufft.
examples.tr: In the organic shop amaranth is mostly sold as grains or puffed.

examples.text: Roter Amarant färbt das Kochwasser rot.
examples.tr: Red amaranth turns the cooking water red.

synonyms.nuance: German folk name of the genus, after the long flower spikes
spelling variant, as in English

etymology.text: Borrowed from Latin amarantus, from Ancient Greek ἀμάραντος (amárantos, “unfading”); the spelling Amaranth is influenced by ἄνθος (ánthos, “flower”).

funFacts: Greek βλίτα (vlíta), boiled amaranth greens with lemon and oil, is a classic summer dish; Chinese 苋菜 (xiàncài) is amaranth greens too.
Amaranth was a staple grain of the Aztecs.
pitfalls: Gender: Wiktionary gives der Amarant (also das); the colour amaranth is das Amarant.
In German Amarant usually means the grain; for the vegetable say Amarantblätter.
subtleties: The same plants give grain (the seeds) and greens (the leaves); some species are common garden weeds.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A peppery green you can pick in winter, when little else grows.

senses.def: winter cress, land cress (Barbarea vulgaris, Barbarea verna), eaten like watercress

examples.text: Winterkresse schmeckt scharf wie Brunnenkresse.
examples.tr: Land cress tastes peppery like watercress.

examples.text: Die Winterkresse kann man auch im Dezember ernten.
examples.tr: You can harvest land cress even in December.

examples.text: Ein paar Blätter Winterkresse machen den Salat würziger.
examples.tr: A few leaves of land cress make the salad spicier.

synonyms.nuance: name after Saint Barbara (feast day 4 December)
the species usually grown as land cress, Barbarea verna

etymology.text: From Winter (“winter”) + Kresse (“cress”, from Old High German kressa, cognate with English cress).

funFacts: Barbarakraut is named after Saint Barbara, whose feast day falls in early winter, when the plant can still be picked.
pitfalls: Strictly, Winterkresse is Barbarea vulgaris; the land cress of seed catalogues is the related Barbarea verna. Both are eaten the same way.
subtleties: Older leaves become bitter; pick young ones or the winter rosettes.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A curious onion that grows little onions on top of its stalk, storey above storey.

senses.def: tree onion, walking onion, Egyptian onion (Allium × proliferum)

examples.text: Die Etagenzwiebel bildet oben am Stängel kleine Zwiebeln.
examples.tr: The tree onion forms small onions at the top of the stalk.

examples.text: Die kleinen Etagenzwiebeln kann man einlegen.
examples.tr: The small tree onions can be pickled.

examples.text: Etagenzwiebeln sind ganz einfach zu vermehren.
examples.tr: Tree onions are very easy to propagate.

collocations.tr: the bulblets of the tree onion

synonyms.nuance: name after the bulblets in the air
loan translation of English Egyptian onion

etymology.text: Etage (“storey, floor”, borrowed from French étage) + Zwiebel (“onion”, from Old High German zwibollo, from Late Latin cēpulla).

funFacts: English calls it walking onion: the heavy stalks bend, the bulblets touch the ground and root, so the plant “walks” across the bed.
pitfalls: Etage is pronounced the French way: [eˈtaːʒə].
subtleties: You can eat the green leaves like spring onions and the bulblets like small onions or shallots.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: A lettuce grown for its thick, crunchy stem, a favourite in China, almost unknown in Germany.

senses.def: celtuce, stem lettuce: a form of lettuce (Lactuca sativa) grown for its thick stem
asparagus salad (a dish)

examples.text: Beim Spargelsalat isst man vor allem den dicken Stängel.
examples.tr: With celtuce you mainly eat the thick stem.

examples.text: Spargelsalat ist in China ein beliebtes Gemüse.
examples.tr: Celtuce is a popular vegetable in China.

examples.text: Samen für Spargelsalat bekommt man im Gartenversand.
examples.tr: You can get celtuce seeds from garden mail-order shops.

examples.text: Zum Schnitzel gibt es heute Spargelsalat mit Erdbeeren.
examples.tr: Today the schnitzel comes with asparagus salad with strawberries.

synonyms.nuance: the English name, used in seed catalogues
descriptive name, also Stiel-Salat

etymology.text: Spargel (“asparagus”, from Medieval Latin sparagus) + Salat (“lettuce, salad”, from earlier Italian salata).

funFacts: Chinese 莴笋 (wōsǔn): the peeled stem is sliced and stir-fried or eaten cold with sesame oil.
pitfalls: Spargelsalat also means a salad made of asparagus – context decides.
subtleties: The stem is peeled because the skin is bitter; the leaves are edible but less valued.

homonyms.none: no other noun with this form

profile.feeling: Tiny white onions in a jar of mixed pickles or on a cocktail stick.

senses.def: pearl onion, a very small mild onion, usually pickled

examples.text: Im Glas mit Mixed Pickles sind auch Perlzwiebeln.
examples.tr: There are pearl onions in the jar of mixed pickles too.

examples.text: Zum Raclette gibt es Perlzwiebeln und Gewürzgurken.
examples.tr: With raclette there are pearl onions and pickled gherkins.

examples.text: Perlzwiebeln lassen sich nach kurzem Blanchieren leicht schälen.
examples.tr: Pearl onions are easy to peel after brief blanching.

synonyms.nuance: trade name for small white pickling onions; often used for the same product

etymology.text: Perle (“pearl”, from Old High German perala, from Vulgar Latin *perla) + Zwiebel (“onion”).

funFacts: A cocktail called the Gibson is a martini garnished with a pearl onion instead of an olive.
pitfalls: Botanically German Wikipedia treats the Perlzwiebel as a form of Allium ampeloprasum (the leek species); in shops any tiny white onion is sold as Perlzwiebel or Silberzwiebel.
subtleties: Almost always used in the plural: one onion alone is rarely mentioned.

profile.feeling: Garlic heads as big as a fist, but mild – a show-off at the market.

senses.def: elephant garlic (Allium ampeloprasum), a large, mild garlic-like bulb

examples.text: Elefantenknoblauch hat riesige Zehen.
examples.tr: Elephant garlic has huge cloves.

examples.text: Elefantenknoblauch schmeckt viel milder als normaler Knoblauch.
examples.tr: Elephant garlic tastes much milder than normal garlic.

examples.text: Gerösteter Elefantenknoblauch wird weich und süß.
examples.tr: Roasted elephant garlic becomes soft and sweet.

synonyms.nuance: descriptive shop name
the wild species Allium ampeloprasum (German Wikipedia), of which elephant garlic is a form

etymology.text: Elefant (“elephant”, from Middle High German elefant, Old High German helfant) + Knoblauch (“garlic”, from Old High German chlobalouh, “clove-leek”).

funFacts: Despite the name it is closer to leek than to garlic: it is a form of the same species as the leek.
pitfalls: Like Knoblauch it has no plural in normal use: say Knollen (bulbs) or Zehen (cloves).
subtleties: Because it is mild, it is often roasted whole or sliced raw, where normal garlic would be too strong.

profile.feeling: A pale, slim winter root that smells of parsley: soups and Sunday stews.

senses.def: root parsley, Hamburg parsley (Petroselinum crispum var. tuberosum) and its root

examples.text: Petersilienwurzeln geben der Suppe ein feines Aroma.
examples.tr: Root parsley gives the soup a delicate flavour.

examples.text: Die Petersilienwurzel sieht aus wie eine kleine Pastinake.
examples.tr: Root parsley looks like a small parsnip.

examples.text: In Österreich gehört die Petersilienwurzel ins Wurzelgemüse für die Rindsuppe.
examples.tr: In Austria root parsley belongs in the root vegetables for beef soup.

synonyms.nuance: the plant variety (Wiktionary: root parsley); Petersilienwurzel is the usual market name for the root

etymology.text: Petersilie (“parsley”, from Old High German petarsilia) + -n- + Wurzel (“root”).

funFacts: It is the same species as leaf parsley, bred for the root – its leaves can be used like parsley too.
pitfalls: Easy to confuse with Pastinake (parsnip): the parsnip is bigger, sweeter, and has a sunken leaf base; root parsley smells of parsley.
subtleties: Wiktionary also lists Petersilienwurzel for the root of ordinary leaf parsley; at the market it means the special root variety.
